citation_review.method: Manual source review against exact supplied historical ranges. A fully supported citation set covers every positive code-behavior claim and includes no unrelated citation. Missing-source observations are checked against the entire supplied prompt. This is separate from source-ID/range validity; no automatic semantic scorer is claimed.

acceptance.decision: Keep experimental repository opt-in; no broader rollout or token-saving claim.

limitations: Six scoped before/after probes, one native invocation per arm except budget-failed retries; not whole-PR reviews or a statistical quality benchmark.
The 8 KiB assigned excerpts omit CreateTokenDialog lifecycle in both token-dialog cases; production initial analysis receives the complete assigned file.
The assessment native task adds finding/history instructions, while this scoped harness supplies no finding history. Some responses request history for that reason.
Source text carries start/end metadata but no inline line numbers. Citation accuracy is poor; production evidence gates were not exercised by this custom verdict schema.
Python absolute imports are unresolved, so jobs graph and baseline prompts are identical. Token differences for these prompts are execution variability, not retrieval savings.
Graph selection misses the combobox wrapper for the SearchSelect defect under its frozen ordering/caps. No post-result retrieval tuning or relabeling was performed.
Source expansion rounds are zero: required_paths are recorded but not executed. Internal provider inference rounds and separate input/output tokens are not exposed by this transport.
Latency covers native runner requests only, excludes corpus preparation, GitHub authorization and approval pauses; p95 uses nearest rank over a tiny sample.
Subscription tokens are reported aggregate consumption, not monetary API cost. Failed token-limit attempts count in spend but their discarded answers cannot be scored.
